To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
oxidative stress activates two distinct pathways that lead to phosphorylation of Akt in T lymphocytes.

oxidative stress induces the phosphorylation of both T308 and S473 of Akt, that the phosphorylation of S472 is largely PI3 kinase dependent, that the phosphorylations of both T308 are largely CaM-K dependent, that the Src family kinases p56(Lck), p59(Fyn), and p60(Csk) have a role in oxidative stress induced Akt phosphorylation, and that the phosphorylation at S472 is largely Src kinase dependent.
hydrogen peroxide-induced activation of Akt in Jurkat T cells involves two pathways, one involving CaMKs and the other involving PI3K, Src, and CaMK.
In summary, our research is concerned with
elucidating the molecular pathways that lead to the activation of Akt and other signaling pathways by oxidative stress in human T lymphocytes.
the molecular mechanisms that lead to oxidative stress-induced Akt phosphorylation and the potential roles of this phosphorylation in oxidative stress-induced cell death.
the molecular mechanisms by which oxidative stress activates Akt in Jurkat cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
oxidative stress-induced phosphorylations on T308 and S473 are independent of each other and involve different signaling molecules and pathways.
the phosphorylation of T-308 is largely CaM-K-dependent and independent of PI3K activity, whereas the phosphorylation of S-473 is CaM-K-, PI3K-, and Src-dependent.
oxidative stress-induced Akt phosphorylation on S473 is dependent on both CaM-K and PI3K, whereas oxidative stress-induced Akt T308 phosphorylation is largely independent of PI3K.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
hydrogen peroxide-induced Akt activation involves two distinct signaling pathways.
the CaM-K pathway and the PI3K pathway are two independent pathways that can converge to phosphorylate Akt on both S473 and T306.
hydrogen peroxide-induced activation of Akt requires CaM-K activity, PI3K activity, and p56(Lck).
The main takeaway from our work is that
oxidative stress can activate two distinct pathways that converge to phosphorylate Akt on serine473 and threonine 307.
the activation of Akt by oxidative stress is a multifactorial event that involves both the PI3K and the CaM-K pathways.
the phosphorylation of S 473 and T 308 in Akt in response to hydrogen peroxyde is dependent on two different signaling pathways, one involving the CaM-K and the other involving the PI3K and Src.
